children: Sikorsky unit has been selected to supply S-92A+ helicopters for South Korea’s Presidential Helicopter II program, the company announced. The aircraft will serve the Republic of Korea Air Force.

For investors, the selection adds demand for Sikorsky’s upgraded S-92 platform and includes equipment and maintenance support that could generate revenue beyond aircraft deliveries. The announcement did not disclose the contract’s value, the number of helicopters ordered or a delivery schedule, limiting assessment of its financial impact.

image.alt: Rendering courtesy of Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company.

children: Korea Aviation Engineering & Maintenance Service, a Korea Aerospace Industries subsidiary, will install mission equipment in South Korea. The contract also covers additional special mission equipment, spare parts and field service support.
The South Korean air force received three S-92 helicopters in 2007 for presidential transport. Other South Korean agencies use the platform for search and rescue, firefighting and emergency response.

The S-92A+ features upgraded engines and a redesigned main gearbox, with capacity to carry more payload or fuel. The S-92 also forms the basis of the U.S. Marine Corps’ VH-92A presidential helicopter.
Sikorsky said it is increasing S-92A+ production at facilities in Stratford, Connecticut, and Owego, New York, with capacity to manufacture up to 12 aircraft a year.

title: South Korea selects Sikorsky for presidential helicopter program
